title: Feature-detection kit
blurb: Runs four independent toneMapping detectors (dictionary getter read, enum validation, default reflection, extended reflection) to separate false positives from reliable HDR branching.
question: Which capability probe reliably detects active Canvas2D extended tone mapping without false positives from builds that reflect a constant default?
result: In Chrome 153 flag-off, default reflection returns true while memberRead, enumValidated, and reflectsExtended return false; with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, memberRead and enumValidated become true while reflectsExtended stays false. Only verifying that requesting 'extended' reflects 'extended' avoids false positives.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36 (Linux, headless, SDR) with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features on 2026-11-28; earlier Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12

friction.summary: Checking 'toneMapping' in ctx.getContextAttributes() is a false positive on Chrome 153 with the feature off
friction.repro: Create a default 2D context in Chrome 153 without flags and read getContextAttributes().toneMapping; it returns { mode: 'standard' } even though the creation option is never read and invalid enum values do not throw.
